gaps.sentence: She ___ her keys again — this is the third time this month!
gaps.hint: third time this month connects to now
gaps.explanation: 'This is the third time' links a recent event to now, so the present perfect is required: has lost.

gaps.sentence: When she was a student, she ___ spend her summers hitchhiking around Europe.
gaps.hint: a repeated past action with would
gaps.explanation: 'Would' describes repeated past actions in narrative: would spend.

gaps.sentence: She ___ me yesterday to say she had arrived safely.
gaps.hint: yesterday fixes a finished past action
gaps.explanation: 'Yesterday' is a finished past time, so the past simple is used: phoned.

gaps.sentence: He ___ in the garden when the storm broke.
gaps.explanation: An action in progress interrupted by a short event — past continuous.

gaps.sentence: By the time I woke up, my flatmates ___ to work.
gaps.hint: by the time plus past simple
gaps.explanation: 'By the time' plus a past action refers back to an earlier past action, so the past perfect is needed: had gone.

gaps.sentence: The bridge ___ to traffic every year for repainting in May.
gaps.explanation: A recurring scheduled event takes the present simple.

gaps.sentence: She ___ three novels since she retired.
gaps.explanation: 'Since she retired' (up to now) — present perfect.

gaps.sentence: Why ___ sunglasses? It is dark in here.
gaps.hint: happening now with a visible reason
gaps.explanation: The speaker asks about something visibly happening now, so the present continuous fits: are you wearing.
